title: Monospace face — six candidates against Anek Latin
type_note: Same declared stretch of 'competitive-benchmark' as ART-006: the subject is six typefaces competing for one role, not six companies. Structure matches — named dimensions, measured, with a verdict.

capture.method: Chrome DevTools MCP. Advance uniformity measured across 'i I l 1 O 0 m W x .' via canvas TextMetrics at 200px weight 400; x-height from actualBoundingBoxAscent of 'x', cap-height from 'H'. Each family confirmed loaded via document.fonts.check before measurement so no figure is a silent fallback. Anek Latin measured in the same pass as the pairing reference.

sources.what: Source Code Pro, Space Mono, DM Mono, IBM Plex Mono, Roboto Mono, JetBrains Mono — all SIL OFL, served by Google Fonts, weights 400/500/700
Anek Latin — the pairing reference, measured in the same pass

decision_note: Source Code Pro selected on optical pairing — x-height 0.486 against Anek Latin's 0.488, a 0.4% difference, 14x closer than the nearest rival. Unlike ART-006, the measurement and the brand preference agreed here, so no override was needed. Recorded explicitly because the coincidence is worth not mistaking for a rule: had IBM Plex Mono won on measurement, the 'Not IBM' argument would have had to be made in the open rather than carried by a metric.
provenance_note: sha256 null for both sources: Google Fonts serves a per-user-agent subset, so a hash would fix this session's slice rather than the family. The measurements and the stated method are the evidence, not the binaries. Found by validation/audit-contracts.py, which flagged typography.scale.code as byte-identical to caption.
